fact: Benin's Ministry of Economy and Finance circular of 25 September 2026 institutes electronic payment of official-mission expenses in all public administrations, with the SEMO 2 modules ready for domestic implementation.

The government says the GBESSOKE productive social safety-net programme is in a pilot phase across 12 communes, with electronic transfers to households received on secured SIM cards and extension planned to all 77 communes.

The government says GBESSOKE began monthly cash transfers on 18 September 2025, paying 20,621 beneficiaries (85% women) a first instalment of 208,272,100 FCFA, received on their mobile phones via secured SIM cards.

A Ministry of Economy and Finance communique says pensions under 50,000 FCFA are paid into beneficiaries' mobile money accounts from the 1 November 2020 instalment, and the government says over 3,700 pensioners (30% of those expected) were paid that way in that instalment.

Pensions of 50,000 FCFA or more are paid by bank transfer, which Fonds national des retraites du Benin pensioners have had for some years and Caisse nationale de securite sociale pensioners now have, per the article.
